The proposed cubic-subproblem solver omits the hard case. Lemma 2 establishes monotonicity only for shifts strictly above the negative minimum eigenvalue; it does not guarantee that the proposed lower bracket exists. For example, when the gradient is zero and the Hessian has negative curvature, the inverse-based solution is zero for every admissible shift, while a cubic-model minimizer requires a nonzero negative-curvature step at the boundary shift. Increasing the cubic regularizer does not eliminate this issue.

Strict positivity of individual iterates does not itself establish a uniform positive lower bound over all iterations and trial queries. A rigorous feasible-step and level-set argument is needed, together with bounds on the resulting smoothness constants. Their dependence on sample size, barrier strength, and target accuracy, as well as the cost and accuracy of inner solves, is missing from the advertised total runtime.

Global clustering optimality remains conditional on Assumption 1, with evidence limited to successful runs from selected initializations. Furthermore, the positive-barrier objective on U differs from the SDP barrier on Z, and finite positive barrier strength excludes the exact block membership matrix. The paper needs a quantitative connection between barrier strength, stationarity tolerance, rounding, and recovery accuracy. Zero label error alone does not certify global optimality of the continuous objective, and the reference used for the plotted 'global suboptimality' is insufficiently specified.
